prompt:
Add status --json and document it in CLI help. Successful JSON status emits only one JSON object on stdout, no stderr, exit 0, deterministic for unchanged state. Exact version-1 schema (no extra fields): {"schemaVersion":1,"stateFile":<actual state.json path>,"tools":[{"name":"codex","ownedFiles":<integer>},{"name":"claude","ownedFiles":<integer>}],"cursorMode":"project-local"}. Tool array order must be codex then claude. Preserve existing ownership counts: count recorded paths under ToolRoot (.codex or .claude), even if files are missing; Codex .agents/skills paths do not count. Prefix sibling directories do not count. Missing state gives zero counts without creating state. Preserve ordinary status output byte-for-byte and existing malformed-JSON controlled exit-2 behavior with no partial JSON output. Reject --json on other commands before work. This task does not add semantic ownership-state validation. Keep all existing public APIs available; exercise behavior through HarnessApp.Run in the existing executable test project, not newly added test helper APIs. Add focused regression coverage. Do not change project files, dependencies, models.conf, instructions, embedded assets, or unrelated behavior. Run the existing .NET test suite. Only src/AgentHarness/*.cs and tests/AgentHarness.Tests/*.cs may change.
Validation: dotnet run --project tests/AgentHarness.Tests/AgentHarness.Tests.csproj --configuration Release --disable-build-servers -p:UseSharedCompilation=false. The fixture fixes offline package sources and isolated compilation identically for both instruction versions. Do not modify build configuration. Work only in this fixture and its supplied workflow instructions; do not inspect other trials or benchmark/grader files.
Argument boundary v2: validate --tools values in both --tools VALUE and --tools=VALUE forms before command work. Reject missing, empty/whitespace and option-shaped values (beginning with a hyphen after trimming leading whitespace) with exit 2 and an argument diagnostic, even for commands that do not otherwise use Tools. A standalone --json token must be rejected on every non-status command, including help aliases, before generic parsing can consume it as another option's value. status --tools --json and status --tools=--json are invalid; they must not emit JSON. Valid tool values and ordinary help behavior without --json remain compatible. No state reads/writes, project writes, downloads or executable replacement may precede these rejections. Errors must identify the malformed --tools or --json option, rather than reporting a state error or an unrelated required option.
